title: Multi-protocol tool routing and stable identifier spec
creator: Sofia Patel
description: We need a deterministic way to route tool/function calls coming from multiple client protocols (OpenAI-style tool specs, legacy 'function' payloads, and internal SDKs) to the correct runtime backend variant. This ticket defines a stable identifier scheme, routing precedence, and translation rules so the runtime can resolve calls with predictable fallbacks and reliable telemetry.
proposal: Introduce a canonical-tool-id (ctid) that is generated and persisted when a tool/function is onboarded. Build a lightweight protocol fingerprint layer that maps incoming protocol shapes (openai_tool, legacy_fn, internal_rpc) to candidate ctid(s). Routing rules: 1) Exact ctid match -> native backend; 2) Protocol-fingerprint match -> mapped backend; 3) Heuristic aliasing fallback with confidence score; 4) Explicit deny/require flags for security-sensitive tools. The runtime exposes an API to query ctid metadata and translation history.
acceptance_criteria: Runtime can resolve calls from OpenAI-style tool payloads to a ctid with >=99.5% accuracy on the integration test set
A deterministic fallback chain is recorded in telemetry for every routed call
There is a migration runbook to backfill ctids for existing legacy functions without downtime
CLI/SDK exposes a lookup endpoint to show canonical id, aliases, and protocol mappings
implementation_plan: Design ctid format and storage model (prefix, hash, human alias)
Implement protocol fingerprint matcher in the routing layer (configurable thresholds)
Add mapping table in metadata service and migration tool to generate ctids for existing tools
Instrument telemetry: resolution path, confidence score, chosen backend, and latency impact
Write compatibility tests exercising openai-tool -> legacy-fn -> internal-sdk scenarios
Ship SDK helper to annotate calls with preferred ctid to short-circuit resolution
risks: Mis-resolution causing a tool to execute against an incompatible backend (sanity checks required)
Performance overhead in hot-path routing if fingerprint matcher is not optimized
Backfill generating identifier churn if not idempotent; could break cached references
Edge cases for streaming calls where mid-stream switching is required (requires additional signals)
notes: We intentionally avoid protocol-specific IDs (eg. openai:send_file) being first-class in routing; ctids are the single source of truth
Plan to persist a small alias list per ctid for human-friendly lookup and backward compat
Migration should include a read-through cache on routing layer to minimize queries to metadata service
Security teams requested an allowlist mode for admin-only tools (will gate by metadata flag)
